title: Greenfield CLI: word-frequency counter with tests
prompt:
Create a Python command-line tool in this workspace. Requirements:

1. Create a file named exactly `wordfreq.py` at the workspace root.
2. It reads a text file whose path is given as the first positional argument and prints the most common words, one per line, in the exact format `word: count` (the word, then a colon, a space, then the count).
3. Words are case-insensitive (lowercase them) and are sequences of alphanumeric characters (split on any non-alphanumeric character; ignore empty tokens).
4. Sort by count descending; break ties alphabetically (ascending).
5. Print the top 10 by default. Support a `--top N` flag to change how many are printed.
6. Also create `test_wordfreq.py` with pytest tests covering: basic counting, the --top flag, case-insensitivity, and tie-breaking.
7. Ensure `python -m pytest test_wordfreq.py` passes.

When done, the command `python wordfreq.py <file> --top 3` must print exactly the top 3 words in the format above.
